findings.title: CNCMachineRMS: The Undocumented RAT At the End of a BabaDeda Chain
findings.summary_md: LevelBlue SpiderLabs documented CNCMachineRMS as a previously undocumented 1.14 MB x64 remote access trojan at the end of a BabaDeda loader chain. The chain starts with a ClickFix lure, abuses a legitimately signed IBM SPSS IDE executable named WinWrapIDE.exe through COM, loads four decoy DLLs, and uses EnumTimeFormatsEx as a trampoline for shellcode. The implant has no import table, resolves APIs by hash, builds strings on the stack, and provides an interactive shell, file manager, screen capture, local account backdoor, seven persistence mechanisms and twenty typed commands. LevelBlue reported a screenshot on first contact and 600-second beacons.

findings.title: CNCMachineRMS C2 Protocol
findings.summary_md: Netresec traced the CNCMachineRMS binary command-and-control protocol to packet captures from Brad Duncan in April 2026, where ClickFix fake CAPTCHA pages delivered a RAT talking to 89.110.110.119 over TCP port 443 without TLS. FlowCarp identified additional C2 servers on port 443: 85.158.110.78, 89.124.79.98 and 144.124.242.171. The post documents DNS over HTTPS lookups for notepadreleased[.]com through dns.google, cloudflare-dns.com and dns.quad9.net just before C2 connections, so local DNS logs can miss the lookup. It lists 89.110.110.119:443 as first seen 2026-04-06 and last seen 2026-05-27.

findings.title: Attackers Abuse ChatGPT Custom GPTs to Deliver RAT via ClickFix
findings.summary_md: Huntress documented two malicious Custom GPTs that pushed victims from sponsored ChatGPT results to Google Sites pages posing as Cloudflare checks. The ClickFix command downloaded ISOSimple.msi, which sideloaded code through a Canon-signed COTFileReadApp.exe and established Run key and scheduled-task persistence named Canon Configuration Reader. The SOC handled at least 40 incidents from the Google Sites domain, two confirmed as Custom GPT driven, and found a replacement GPT on 2026-09-27 after OpenAI took down the first on 2026-09-25. A 2026-10-14 update described a shift to gptverification[.]com and new Google Sites pages.

findings.title: ROMULUS: Analysis of a New Multi-Payload ClickFix Delivery Platform
findings.summary_md: Forescout Vedere Labs named ROMULUS a reusable multi-payload ClickFix delivery platform discovered while investigating infrastructure tied to the Custom GPT campaign. The research described separate infection chains, one delivering a RAT through a Stardock installer and another delivering LegionLoader through a PowerShell script, and identified six IP addresses hosting ROMULUS panels through VirusTotal and Shodan pivots. One server overlapped with infrastructure already reported by Huntress.

findings.title: CNCMachineRMS: The Missing Piece in the ROMULUS Campaign
findings.summary_md: Blackpoint APG identified the previously unnamed RAT delivered by ROMULUS as CNCMachineRMS, matching a SHA-256 from Huntress, family strings and an identical 1,128-entry storage archive with 315 directories and 813 files. In the Stardock chain, IconEdit2Turb.msi dropped a modified DeElevator64.dll and I++u.dll, which decrypted roughly 341 KB of shellcode from Build.dat and ran it through EnumSystemCodePagesW; the controller script was 3,904 bytes and the final RAT about 1.58 MB. Persistence used a Run key and scheduled task named Stardock DeElevation Tool, reasserted every 150 and 875 seconds, with C2 resolution over DNS over HTTPS. Blackpoint observed no post-exploitation activity and assessed ROMULUS as a delivery service distributing CNCMachineRMS and LegionLoader through separate chains.
